Title: Celtics' Payton Pritchard set to benefit from new NBA rule

Summary: 
Payton Pritchard, a guard for the Boston Celtics, is set to benefit from a new NBA rule effective with the 2025-26 season. The rule, tested in the G League, states that any shot taken from at least 36 feet within the final three seconds of the first three quarters—provided it originates in the backcourt—will be counted as a team shot attempt, not an individual one. This change prevents such shots from negatively affecting a player’s individual shooting percentage. Pritchard has long been known for taking deep heaves at the end of quarters, logging 11 such shots from 36+ feet in the 2024-25 season, all of which missed (0-for-11). Of these, seven would now be classified as team misses under the new rule. This would improve his hypothetical 3-point percentage from 40.7% (255-for-626) to 41.2% (255-for-619). Pritchard, who previously dismissed concerns over shooting percentages as 'soft mentally,' stated he would have taken the shots regardless but acknowledged the rule could help his stats. The NBA implemented the rule to discourage players from taking late, long-range shots after the buzzer, a behavior Pritchard has consistently avoided. His buzzer-beating 3-pointer in Game 5 of the 2024 NBA Finals remains a defining moment in Celtics lore.

Title: NBA | 鼓勵搏大霧 每節臨完「浪射」不計出手次數

Summary: 
The NBA has introduced a rule change that will affect how end‑of‑quarter long‑range shots are recorded.  From the start of the new season, shots taken in the final seconds of a quarter that are attempted from a very long distance—often called a "deep‑threat" or "wave shot"—will be counted as a team attempt but will not be included in a player’s individual statistics.  This change, approved by the league owners’ meeting and reported by ESPN, is intended to encourage more players to take these high‑risk shots even though the probability of making them is low; a successful shot still yields three points, while a miss has no penalty.

The league also announced two additional procedural changes.  First, starting this season, if a coach challenges a boundary call, the decision will be made by the replay‑center referee rather than the on‑floor chief referee, speeding up the review process.  Second, the format of the NBA Cup will shift beginning with the 2026‑27 season: the final will be played at a neutral venue (Las Vegas), while the quarterfinals will be hosted by the higher‑seeded teams in each conference.  The 2025‑26 season will retain the current model, with both the quarterfinals and final held in Las Vegas.

The league highlighted the desire to see more players like Boston’s Payton Pritchard, who specialize in end‑of‑quarter long‑range attempts, as a way to increase the spectacle of the game.  The new rule is expected to make the end of each quarter more exciting for fans while preserving the integrity of individual player statistics.

The NBA's new 'heave' rule for emergency long-range shots, implemented in the 2025-26 season, has shown significant impact. Payton Pritchard, the Celtics' backup point guard and 'Best Sixth Man,' previously criticized players who prioritize personal shooting percentage over team victory, calling it a 'weak mindset.' However, the league's emphasis on three-point efficiency has made hesitation understandable. The rule change appears to be 'targeted and effective,' as players are now more willing to shoot without fear of negative personal stats. Fans now see nearly one such long-range attempt per game on average. Last season, Nikola Jokić and Stephen Curry each led the league with three successful long-range heaves.

Title: Are Celtics Sounding Alarm On Disastrous 0-3 Start Not Seen Since 2013-14 Season?

Summary: 
The Boston Celtics have started the 2025 NBA season with a 0-3 record for the first time since the 2013-14 season, following a 119-113 loss to the Detroit Pistons on October 27, 2025. Jaylen Brown led all scorers with 41 points, while Derrick White added 15 and Anfernee Simons contributed 12 off the bench. Despite a 14-2 opening lead and a 17-point advantage at one point, the Celtics faltered in the second half due to defensive lapses and rebounding issues, which have been consistent across all three losses. Head coach Joe Mazzulla emphasized the need for effort to align with execution, stating, 'We gotta close the second quarter better. Obviously, the fouls and the rebounds.' Guard Payton Pritchard, who scored 21 points, acknowledged the unfamiliar adversity, saying, 'This is my first time really going on a three-game losing streak. So it's unfamiliar. It's a little adversity. So you look at this and you use it to make us better.' The team is operating without Jayson Tatum, Jrue Holiday, Kristaps Porzingis, and Al Horford, forcing a smaller, guard-heavy rotation and reliance on new players. Despite the struggles, the Celtics view the losing streak as a wake-up call and a test of character, with Pritchard suggesting that 'a little adversity' may be necessary to spark a turnaround.

Published date: October 27 2025, 17:31
